q.q: Which component acts as the main circuit board connecting all parts of the computer, such as the CPU, RAM, and storage?
q.x: The motherboard is the main printed circuit board (PCB) that provides electrical connectivity and communication pathways between all hardware components.

q.q: Which unit is used to measure the clock speed of a processor?
q.x: Clock speed is measured in Hertz (Hz), commonly expressed in Megahertz (MHz) or Gigahertz (GHz). It indicates how many cycles a processor can execute per second.

q.q: Which hardware device is classified as an input device?
q.x: A keyboard allows a user to enter data and commands into a computer, making it an input device. Monitors, printers, and speakers are categorized as output devices.

q.q: Which type of port is most commonly used to connect modern peripherals like mice, keyboards, and printers?
q.x: Universal Serial Bus (USB) is the standard industry interface for connecting a wide range of peripherals. It replaced older, slower ports like Parallel and PS/2.

q.q: Which hardware device is used to produce a hard copy of a digital document?
q.x: A printer is an output device that translates electronic files into physical documents on paper. Scanners are input devices, while joysticks and microphones are used for control and audio input.

q.q: What is the primary function of a Power Supply Unit (PSU) in a desktop computer?
q.x: The PSU takes high-voltage Alternating Current (AC) from a wall outlet and converts it into low-voltage Direct Current (DC) required by computer components. Without this conversion, the sensitive internal parts would be damaged.

q.q: Which of the following is considered volatile memory?
q.x: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile, meaning it requires power to maintain the stored information. When the computer is turned off, data in the RAM is lost.

q.q: Which of the following describes an Optical Disk drive?
o: A device that reads data using laser beams
A device that uses magnetic fields to store bits
A device that performs complex calculations
A device that handles network traffic
q.x: Optical drives like CD, DVD, or Blu-ray drives use laser light to read data from or write data to a reflective disk surface. This is distinct from magnetic or electronic storage.

q.q: What is the function of the CMOS battery on a motherboard?
o: To maintain system date and time settings
q.x: The CMOS battery provides the necessary power to the BIOS chip to store system settings, including the current date and time, even when the computer is unplugged.

q.q: Which storage medium uses magnetic platters to store data?
q.x: Traditional Hard Disk Drives (HDDs) utilize spinning magnetic platters and read/write heads to store and retrieve data. SSDs, conversely, use flash memory chips.

q.q: Which hardware component is primarily responsible for performing arithmetic and logical operations in a computer?
q.x: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) is the part of the CPU that handles mathematical calculations and logical comparisons. It is the core functional unit responsible for processing data.

q.q: What is the primary purpose of a Heat Sink in a computer system?
q.x: A heat sink is a passive component designed to absorb and dissipate heat away from the processor. This prevents the CPU from overheating and maintaining performance stability.
